title: Maximal-branch strictification with smooth relative charts over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $X$ an integral smooth finite-type $F$-scheme [def-weil-field, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $B\subset X$ be a reduced effective Cartier divisor such that etale locally at each geometric point there is a smooth $F$-map $c:V	o\mathbf A^r_F$ with $B	imes_XV=c^{-1}V(z_1\cdots z_r)$, all $r$ branches passing through the point [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Allow self-intersections of global components. Let a finite group $J$ act compatibly on $F,X$ preserving $B$, possibly nontrivially on $F$. There exists a finite $J$-equivariant tower of ordinary blowups $b:X_N	o\cdots	o X_0=X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Put $D_0=B$, $H_0=\varnothing$, let $D_i$ be the strict transform of $B$, and put $B_i=(b_{i,0}^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-nagata-strict-transform, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. At each nonterminal stage $D_i
e\varnothing$, let $m_i$ be its maximal geometric branch count [def-trf-normal-crossings-branch-count]. The center $Z_i$ is the reduced locus with branch count $m_i$, is smooth over $F$, is $J$-invariant, and in a smooth coordinate chart for $B_i$ is given by $(z_1,\ldots,z_{m_i})$, with $D_i=V(z_1\cdots z_{m_i})$. One has $B_i=D_i\cup H_i$ as reduced closed subschemes, and $H_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}(H_i\cup Z_i))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor. Each $X_i$ is integral, regular, smooth and finite type over $F$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]; each $B_i$ has the same kind of smooth coordinate charts. More specifically the $z_j$-chart of the blowup is smooth over the affine space with coordinates $z_j$, $v_k=z_k/z_j$ for $k\le m_i$, $k
e j$, and $z_k$ for $k>m_i$, with reduced full boundary $z_j\prod_{k\le m_i,k
e j}v_k\prod_{k>m_i}z_k=0$. The next old strict transform is empty or has maximum branch count at most $m_i-1$. At the terminal stage $D_N=\varnothing$ and $B_N=H_N$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor over $F$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. If $B
e\varnothing$ then $N\le m_0$; if $B=\varnothing$ one can take $N=0$. Each blowup and their composite are projective in the projective-bundle sense, birational, and isomorphisms away from the boundary [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. When $m_i=1$, the blowup may be the identity but $D_{i+1}=\varnothing$ and $D_i$ is included in $H_{i+1}$. The actions lift to all stages, with the group law respected. No perfection assumption on $F$ is made. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8 pp.117--118 and 4.2.8--4.2.9 pp.120--121, with the explicit coordinate calculation over F required by X Lemma 2.2 p.149. Returned steps 10--12.

proof.text: We inductively keep $X_i$ integral, smooth and finite type over $F$, $B_i$ a reduced normal crossings divisor with the stated smooth coordinate charts, $D_i$ a reduced union of its components, and $B_i=D_i\cup H_i$, where $H_i$ is relative strict normal crossings. Initially these hold with $D_0=B$ and $H_0=\varnothing$. Indeed [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts] makes the vanishing boundary coordinates local parameters, so they give normal crossings in [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. Smoothness gives regularity by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], and finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ gives Noetherianity by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The empty family in [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor] represents $H_0$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4, p.117; X definition after Theorem 2.1, p.149; Stacks 056S, 01T1.

proof.text: If $D_i\ne\varnothing$, apply [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] to $(X_i,B_i,D_i)$. It supplies the attained finite maximum $m_i\geq1$, its nonempty reduced closed locus $Z_i$, and the next branch bound. To obtain the stronger relative assertion, use an inductively given smooth chart at a geometric point of $Z_i$, and select its factors belonging to $D_i$. They exist: $D_i\times_{X_i}V$ is reduced by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]; each $V(z_k)$ through the point has a regular, hence domain, local ring there by [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts], so after shrinking it is irreducible. By going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] for the flat maps $B_i\times_{X_i}V\to B_i$ and $D_i\times_{X_i}V\to D_i$, generic points of components map to generic points of components. Since $D_i$ is a union of components of $B_i$, the components of $D_i\times_{X_i}V$ are exactly the $V(z_k)$ whose generic point lies over $D_i$, so $D_i\times_{X_i}V$ is the reduced product of those factors. The coordinate count in [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] shows that exactly $m_i$ such factors vanish there; after shrinking and renumbering, $D_i=V(z_1\cdots z_{m_i})$ and the maximal locus is $V(z_1,\ldots,z_{m_i})$. This intersection is smooth and reduced by [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts]. Uniqueness of reduced induced structure in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies it scheme-theoretically with the pullback of $Z_i$; étale pullback preserves reduced induced closed structure by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. Smoothness of $Z_i/F$ now descends by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness]. Branch count and reduced induced structure are intrinsic, so every element of $J$ preserves $Z_i$, including for semilinear actions.

source.place: VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, p.118, with smooth-coordinate intersections over F; Stacks 036U.

proof.text: Blow up $Z_i$. The comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], so the pullback of this global blowup to each étale boundary chart is its coordinate blowup. Étale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; their pullbacks to $D_i$ are étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Reduced full inverse images are compatible with these charts by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. For the strict-transform comparison, the generic-dominance hypothesis of [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change] holds: on affine opens of $D_i$ and its étale pullback, [lem-sc-flat-going-down] forces the contraction of a minimal prime to be minimal (lift a smaller prime by going down). Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts] with $S=\{1,\ldots,m_i\}$ and $T=\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Its $j$-chart is smooth over affine space with coordinates $z_j,v_k=z_k/z_j$ and the unchanged $z_k$, and gives precisely the full-boundary equation in the statement and the old strict-transform equation $\prod_{k\leq m_i,k\ne j}v_k=0$. These are scheme-theoretic equations, including the empty product when $m_i=1$. Thus every point over the center has the required new smooth chart; away from the center the blowup is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], and the old charts apply. At a chosen point discard factors that are units by shrinking and projecting onto the remaining coordinates. That projection is an affine-space projection, smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and its composite with the smooth chart is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Thus all retained boundary coordinates vanish at the point, as required.

source.place: VIII 4.2.9, p.121; Stacks 0H1H, 0805, and strict-transform closure under flat base change.

proof.text: The center is regular and is locally generated by boundary parameters, as proved in Steps 1--2. Apply [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation] to $(X_i,B_i,H_i,Z_i)$. The induction hypothesis that $H_i$ is relative strict normal crossings implies its regular-component strict normal crossings hypothesis. The result gives regularity of $X_{i+1}$, normal crossings of $B_{i+1}$, and a strict normal crossings union of components $H_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}(H_i\cup Z_i))_{\mathrm{red}}$. It also gives $B_{i+1}=B_i^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H_{i+1}=H_i^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$. Since $B_i=D_i\cup H_i$, strict-transform closure commutes with this finite union: on affine opens its ideal is an intersection of kernels of restrictions to the two open parts. Hence $B_{i+1}=D_{i+1}\cup H_{i+1}$. Here $D_{i+1}$ is the successive strict transform in the sense of [def-nagata-strict-transform]; this includes removal of components contained in the center.

We upgrade the last step's regular strict normal crossings assertion for $H_{i+1}$ to the relative one. Its finitely many regular integral components are, at a chosen point of an étale boundary chart, assigned distinct individual coordinate factors by [lem-trf-etale-component-coordinate-identification]; components missing the point disappear after shrinking. Its required chart equation is a subproduct of the full boundary chart by the going-down argument of Step 2 [lem-sc-flat-going-down], $H_{i+1}$ being a union of components of $B_{i+1}$; this subproduct is a reduced effective Cartier divisor by [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts], so $H_{i+1}$ is effective Cartier by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. Thus the pullback of every scheme-theoretic intersection is exactly the intersection of the assigned coordinate hyperplanes. Those intersections are smooth over $F$ of the expected codimension by [lem-sfb-smooth-coordinate-blowup-charts], both on the new charts and on the unchanged charts away from the center. They descend to smooth intersections by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness]. The codimension assertion already holds globally by [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation]. This verifies every clause of [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor], including the empty subset, whose intersection is $X_{i+1}$. In particular $X_{i+1}/F$ is smooth, without using regular-implies-smooth over an imperfect field.

source.place: VIII 4.2.2(i), p.118, and 4.2.9, p.121; X definition after Theorem 2.1, p.149; Stacks 036U.

proof.text: The ideal of $Z_i$ is nonzero: it is the unit ideal on the nonempty dense complement of $B_i$, which is dense by [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense]. It is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, since on a Noetherian affine open every ideal is finitely generated. Therefore [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry] gives integrality of $X_{i+1}$ and projectivity of $b_i$ in the required convention. It is finite type by [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-relative-ample], so $X_{i+1}/F$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and remains Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $b_i$ is an isomorphism outside $B_i$. Both source and target are integral and this common open is nonempty, hence dense in both; restriction to it identifies their function fields. Thus $b_i$ is birational. No separatedness of $X_i/F$ has been assumed.

source.place: Stacks divisors.tex Tags 02ND and 02NS; morphisms.tex Tags 01T3 and 01T1.

proof.text: For completeness lift the action at every stage, rather than choose separate lifts without a group law. An automorphism preserving the ideal of $Z_i$ induces on the sheaf Rees algebra the degreewise map $a\in\mathcal I^n\mapsto g(a)\in\mathcal I^n$, with the same action on degree zero. Identify the blowup with relative Proj by [lem-sfb-blowup-rees-symmetric-presentation] and apply the graded-equivalence and base-identification clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. This supplies an automorphism over $g:X_i\to X_i$. The homogeneous-localization description in [def-nagata-relative-proj] checks the law: pullback sends a degree-zero fraction $a/f^d$ to $g^*(a)/(g^*f)^d$; two such substitutions are the substitution for the composite pullback, and the identity substitution fixes every fraction. These fractions describe all the standard charts, so the lifted morphisms satisfy the action law and the original field action in degree zero. Reduced total inverse images and strict-transform closures are preserved, so the induction keeps $D_i,H_i,B_i$ invariant.

source.place: VIII 4.1.5 and 4.1.8, pp.117--118; functorial Rees algebra construction, Stacks 02NS.

proof.text: Step 2's branch-drop conclusion [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] gives $m_{i+1}\leq m_i-1$ whenever the next old divisor is nonempty. For $m_i=1$, the single-coordinate chart of Step 3 has strict-transform equation $1=0$, so $D_{i+1}=\varnothing$ even though the blowup is the identity; its old divisor is included in the new $H_{i+1}$ by its defining total inverse image. Induction on the positive integer $m_i$ therefore stops after at most $m_0$ steps. At stopping, $D_N=\varnothing$ and the maintained equality gives $B_N=H_N$, relative strict normal crossings. If $B=\varnothing$, choose the empty tower, $N=0$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.7--4.1.8, p.118; explicit rank-one chart of VIII 4.2.9, p.121.

proof.text: Each $X_i$ is quasi-compact by finite type over $F$, and is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition] successively to the projective blowups to get projectivity of their composite. Its restriction away from the original boundary is the composite of the isomorphisms of Step 6; that open remains nonempty in the integral schemes, so the composite is birational as well. The actions from Step 7 make every map and their composite equivariant. This proves all assertions of the finite tower.

split_report.summary: Split the maximal-branch algorithm into nine steps. Reused the existing absolute branch-stratum and permissible-boundary lemmas and added one statement-only smooth-coordinate blowup calculus lemma. Verified smoothness of centers and every boundary intersection over arbitrary F by smooth coordinates and etale descent, not by perfection; verified semilinear group law on Rees fractions and the Cartier-center stopping case.

tool_uses.why: Smooth F-schemes are regular, without perfection; needed before the absolute maximal-branch lemma, not supplied by the six-functor unit.
Its intrinsic maximum stratum and branch-drop conclusion are generic NC blowup geometry; the relative smoothness is separately proved in this item.
Identifies the maximum-count locus in the given smooth chart, a generic branch-count calculation rather than a trace-formula step.
Reduced induced closed structure commutes with etale pullback; used for centers and reduced full boundaries, not for any trace theorem.
Etale-local source descent for ordinary smooth morphisms is needed for centers and component intersections.
Generic strict-transform comparison under flat chart pullback; its generic-dominance hypothesis is checked by going down.
Ordinary permissible-blowup boundary geometry, including regular global components and pure codimension; relative smoothness is added through coordinate intersections.
Assigns distinct chart factors to the regular global components of the accumulated boundary, to descend each actual component intersection.
Density of the complement of an effective Cartier divisor supplies nonzero center ideals and the dense birational open.
